full_judgment:
8. The learned advocate submitted that the police has been given wide power to arrest and to make search and for that matter to enter any house under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1891 (hereinafter referred to as the Code) as of necessity and that the conduct of the Metropolitan police is guided by the Police Regulation Bengal, 1943 (hereinafter referred to as the Police Regulation) and the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Ordinance 1976 (hereinafter referred to as Ordinance, 1976) and that the police is required to follow the provisions thereof strictly and violation thereof leads to punishment under the prevalent laws. It has been submitted that the framers of police laws were well aware about the nature, character and conduct of the people to be recruited in the police force and apprehended excesses and high handedness to be done by some of the police personnels and that the police force being set up for keeping the law and order situation of the country, as a trained and disciplined force with wide powers, cautions and advices were spelt out, mentioning punishments for offenders, in the Police Regulations as well as in the Ordinance 1976. Referring to sections 4(k) and 4(1) of the Code the learned advocate submitted that "inquiry" and "investigation" can be made only after a case or report with police station has been recorded and in that connection search may be made and that except in the situations mentioned in Section 165 of the Code, no search is permitted to be carried out without a warrant as has been mentioned in a Regulation No. 280 (b) of the Police Regulation and search may be made for recovery of a particular thing related to the case and that regulation No. 280(a) provides that the provisions of Chapter-VII and Sections-102, 103, 165 and 166 of the Code are to be scrupulously followed in conducting a search and that search at night has always been discouraged and that regulation No. 280(e) though says that law does not require a search- to be made only by daylight but provides that searching officer should consider whether a house search should be proceeded by night or whether daylight should be waited and in conducting a search the searching officer should also arrange to cause as little inconvenience as possible to the inmates and that house search at night is permitted only in cases when the delay could frustrate the purpose of search and when there is any possibility of removal of the article for which search is required to be made from the house and in such case forcible entry may also be justified. The learned Advocate taking us through Regulation No. 33 of the Police Regulations and Sections-16(d) and (e) of the Ordinance, 1976, submitted that the laws provide that police should not resort to rudeness, harshness and brutality, which are forbidden for the police, and that the offender police personnels are to be punished by the superior officer whenever such incident is brought to their notice and that police force is required to win the respect and goodwill of the people and secure co-operation from them. 

 13. It appears that in Section 3 Dhaka Metropolitan Police Ordinance 1976 (Ordinance-III of 1976) it has been mentioned that Police Act, 1861 shall not apply to the Dhaka Metropolitan area. In order to clarify this provision we requested Assistance of the learned Deputy Attorney General Mr. Shamsuddin Chowdhury and of Ms. Tania Amir the learned Advocate, and both of them submitted that the Metropolitan Police Ordinance, 1976 is not an exhaustive law and that although it has been mentioned that the Police Act 1861 shall not apply to Dhaka Metropolitan area, yet the functioning of Dhaka Metropolitan Police is being guided and regulated by the Police Regulation Bengal, 1943, which has been framed under the provisions of Police Act 1861 inasmuch as the administration and affairs of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police is regulated by the Police Regulations and there is no other law available for the same. We have also noticed that the issue involved in this rule arises out of a search by police but there is no provision available in the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Ordinance, 1976 as to how search is to be made or should be executed. It appears that in conducting a search the provisions of Code of Criminal Procedure is the basic law that being followed and that there is no conflict in following the provisions of Dhaka Metropolitan Police Ordinance and, those of Police Regulation. Further Section-103 of the Ordinance 1976 provides that nothing in the Ordinance shall construe to prevent any person from being prosecuted and punished under any other law or any offence made punishable or prosecuted and punished and under the Ordinance 1976 for an offence punishable under any other law and all such case shall be subjected to the provisions of section 403 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Section 16 of the Ordinance 1976 provides that in conducting a search the police should refrain from needless rudeness and causing of unnecessary annoyance, and in dealing with women and children the police should act with strict regard to decency and with reasonable gentleness. Sections-51 and 52 of the Ordinance, 1976 provides for punishment with imprisonment with or without fine for police for unlawful entry and search as well as for vexatious search or arrests. The regulation-33 of the Police Regulation Bengal, 1943 cautioned the police to the effect that without public co-operation and support police force cannot work and therefore police should show forbearance, civility and courtesy to all in discharging their duties and that rudeness, harshness and brutality is forbidden for police, for which the superior officers in rank are required to take immediate action against the offenders and the regulation No. 280 of the police provides that in conducting a search the police should scrupulously follow the provisions of law contained in Chapter-VII and Sections-102, 103. 165 and 166 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and should ensure that no article either is introduced in the house or is taken out of the house, beyond the knowledge of the owner or occupier of the house, during any search and that general search without warrant is illegal and can be made only under Section-165 of the Code and that search for any specific and particular article, which is known or reasonably believed to be kept in any particular place or in possession of any particular person, can also be made without warrant, provided that delay in conducting such search may frustrate the recovery and that in conducting a search the police should wait for the daylight and search at night is permissible in cases the delay may frustrate purpose. 

 Regulation No. 280 (a) The law in regard to searches is contained in Chapter VII and section 102 and 103, 165 and 166, Code of Criminal Procedure. These sections must be scrupulously followed. The Officer conducting a search should take precautions to prevent the possibility, on the one hand, of any articles being introduced into the house without the knowledge of the inmates, and on the other, of any articles being taken out of the house while the search is in progress. Search should be made in the presence of the owner or someone on his behalf: ------- 

 4-(1) "Investigation" includes all the proceedings under this Code for the collection of evidence conducted by a police officer or by any person (other than a magistrate) who is authorised by Magistrate in this behalf: 

 Section-103--(1) Before making a  search under this Chapter the officer or other person about o make it shall call upon two or more respectable inhabitants of the locality in which the place to be searched is situate to attend and witness the search any may issue an order in writing to them or any of them so to do. 

 (4) The provisions of this Code as to search warrants and the general provisions as to searches contained in section 102 and section 103 shall, so far as may be apply to a search made under this section. 

 (3) Whenever there is reason  to believe that the delay occasioned by requiring an officer-in-charge of another police station to cause a search to be made under sub-section ( 1 ) might result in evidence of the commission of an offence being concealed or destroyed, it shall be lawful for an officer-in-charge of a police-station or a police officer making an investigation under this Chapter to search, or cause to be searched, any place in the limits of another police-station, in accordance with the provisions of section165, as if such place were within the limits of his own station. 

 (4) Any officer conducting a search under sub-section (3) shall forthwith send notice of the search to the officer-in-charge of the police-station within the limits of which such place is situate, and shall also send with such notice a copy of the list (if any) prepared under section 103, and shall also send to the nearest Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence, copies of the records referred to in section 165, sub-section (1) and (3).
